editorial.headline: Urban Transport: A Clear Route for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers route-bound urban transport, from city buses to other bus services operating within urban routes, with national foreign ownership open to 100%.
editorial.body:
Urban Transport is the activity of carrying people from one place to another within an urban area through services bound to a route. Its practical centre of gravity is city-bus transport, alongside other bus transport operated within routes. The definition is concise, but it establishes an important boundary: this is an urban, route-based transport activity, not a catch-all label for every way people move through a city.

The activity is open across the full recorded business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the classification does not reserve the activity for only large operators or only small local enterprises. A business registering here should be able to describe its real operating model plainly: urban passenger movement, conducted along established routes, with city-bus services and other route-based bus operations at the heart of the scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is open. Foreign ownership may reach 100%, so there is no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The relevant source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In practical terms, the national classification presents a straightforward foreign-investment position: an investor may register an urban, route-bound transport business without a reduced foreign-ownership ceiling being imposed by this record.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Medium-High or High. The honest conclusion is therefore direct: foreign investors can register this activity in Bali today, with no Bali-specific foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition stated in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Foreign investors can register this route-bound urban transport activity in Bali today because it is not caught by the island-wide PMA moratorium.
